summary:
Moonbreakers is a pixel-art lunar mission design game for K–12 students that turns real space engineering into a series of choices with consequences. One to four players take on mission-control roles (Flight Director, Booster Officer, Flight Dynamics Officer and Flight Activities Officer) and pick a difficulty from Clear Skies to No Mercy. Together they choose a rocket, configure its engines, tanks and heat shield, select science instruments, set spacecraft mass, fuel, thrust and orbit, and pick a four-person crew of specialists, all against a shared budget that updates with every decision.

At launch, the team’s choices feed NASA’s General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT), which simulates the actual flight, so players see how their design performs.

This answers the challenge directly. Mission design stops being abstract when students feel how one decision ripples through mass, fuel, cost and risk. Moonbreakers gives young learners a safe place to experiment, fail, redesign and collaborate the way real mission teams do, building STEM, budgeting and teamwork skills in one experience.
details:
Moonbreakers: An Interactive Space Mission Design Game

Moonbreakers is an educational space mission design game developed for the 2026 NASA International Space Apps Challenge in Chicago. Our goal is to make aerospace engineering, scientific exploration, and mission planning more accessible through interactive gameplay.

Space mission design involves complex decisions concerning scientific objectives, spacecraft capabilities, resource allocation, budgets, and engineering constraints. These concepts can be difficult for individuals without an aerospace background to understand. Moonbreakers addresses this challenge by transforming mission design into an engaging, decision-based learning experience.

How Moonbreakers Works

Our game concept allows players to take on the role of mission planners responsible for designing and managing space exploration missions. The planned gameplay incorporates spacecraft and scientific instrument selection, mission personnel, orbital planning, resource management, and launch preparation.

Players can explore how different engineering decisions influence mission outcomes. Difficulty settings are intended to provide accessible experiences for beginners while introducing more demanding challenges for experienced players.

The game also explores the consequences of unsuccessful mission planning. For example, our game-over concept depicts a catastrophic outcome in which Earth becomes uninhabitable, emphasizing the importance of strategic decision-making and mission preparedness.

Technology and Development

Moonbreakers uses Python and the Pygame framework as its planned primary development technologies. GitHub supports version control and collaborative development, while Google Workspace and Discord facilitate project planning, documentation, and communication.

Our team has also developed visual concepts and pixel-art assets to establish a consistent science-fiction aesthetic.

Scientific Foundation

The project draws inspiration from real-world aerospace engineering concepts, including systems engineering, mission design, risk assessment, scientific instrument selection, and engineering trade-offs.

Our brainstorming incorporates knowledge gained through NASA educational experiences, including the L'SPACE Mission Concept Academy.

Creativity and Innovation

Moonbreakers combines interactive storytelling, retro-inspired pixel artwork, and mission-planning challenges to introduce players to the realities of space exploration.

Rather than simply presenting scientific facts, our approach encourages players to experiment, make decisions, evaluate consequences, and learn through experience.

Intended Impact

We hope Moonbreakers will inspire students, educators, aspiring engineers, and space enthusiasts to explore aerospace science and engineering.

By making technical concepts more approachable, our project aims to encourage curiosity, collaboration, critical thinking, and greater participation in STEM education.

Our long-term vision is to expand Moonbreakers into an interactive educational platform that introduces increasingly sophisticated space mission design scenarios.
